source.name: Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics and commonly cited UX laws
source.license: concepts only; source_rule is a short paraphrase in our own words

status_values.covered: stated in DSX knowledge and verified by at least one automated rule
status_values.partial: stated in DSX knowledge, verified only in part or only by judgment

heuristics.source_rule: The interface shows what is happening in a timely manner
heuristics.proposal: Automated rule in the states family (S4): loading-state capture with no indicator (progressbar, skeleton or aria-busy) in the loading region, sev 2.

heuristics.source_rule: Speaks the audience's language and follows real-world order
Every situation entered by mistake has an easy way out
heuristics.proposal: Still missing a check for dialogs without a visible close button: rule in the screen family (next free id, T8), sev 2.

heuristics.source_rule: Same concept, same word, same appearance and same place
Prevent the error before a message is needed
heuristics.proposal: Rule in the layout family (L12): destructive button adjacent (less than 8 px) to the common primary action, sev 2.
Addition to text.mjs or screen.mjs: icon-only button for an action outside a toolbar with no visible label, sev 1 (see wdr-30).

heuristics.source_rule: Shortcuts for experienced users without getting in the way of beginners
heuristics.proposal: No feasible automated rule on the captures; left to judgment (bulk actions and saved filters in operational lists).

heuristics.source_rule: Every element justifies its presence; nothing competes with the main action
Errors say what happened, where, and how to fix it
Help close to the task, searchable and in steps
heuristics.proposal: No automated rule; judgment on complex fields without helper text.

laws.proposal: Rule in the layout family (L13): more than 7 same-level actions in a bar, as the knowledge itself already decides, sev 1.

laws.source_rule: A small, distant target is harder to hit
Working memory holds few items; group them into chunks
laws.proposal: Knowledge addition in psychology-and-laws.md, cognitive load section: name the law, state that the 7±2 figure is not a limit on menu items and that it applies to what must be remembered, not to what is seen.

laws.source_rule: People expect the product to work like the others they already use
Every task has complexity that does not go away; someone (system or person) carries it
laws.proposal: Knowledge addition in psychology-and-laws.md (intrinsic load is already there): name the law and the decision IF the complexity is unavoidable THEN the system absorbs it with defaults and prefilling, not the person.

laws.source_rule: Responses under ~400 ms keep the person's pace
laws.proposal: Knowledge addition in interaction-and-feedback.md, next to the 0.1/1/10 s thresholds: name the ~0.4 s threshold for continuous interaction. No automated rule (captures are static).

laws.source_rule: Elements close together are perceived as a group
Elements within the same boundary are perceived as a group
laws.proposal: Rule in the layout family (L14): card inside a card (borders or backgrounds nested more than 2 levels deep), sev 1, an anti-pattern already cited in visual-hierarchy.md.

laws.source_rule: Similar-looking elements are perceived as serving the same function
An experience is remembered by its peak and its end
laws.proposal: Knowledge addition in psychology-and-laws.md: the end of each journey (success confirmation) and the worst moment (error, waiting) weigh most in memory; link to flows (F1) and to feedback/success-confirmation. Possible rule in the flow family (F6): journey whose last step does not reach a success screen or state, sev 1.

laws.source_rule: What differs from the rest gets noticed and remembered
laws.proposal: Knowledge addition in psychology-and-laws.md: name the effect as the rationale for a single primary (T1) and for the emphasis limit (L2).

laws.source_rule: An interrupted task stays in memory; visible progress helps completion
laws.proposal: Knowledge addition in psychology-and-laws.md linked to forms.md (steps) and interaction-and-feedback.md (setup checklist): show progress and what remains; never use the open task to pressure (dark-patterns.md, nagging).

laws.source_rule: A good-looking interface seems easier and masks problems in testing
laws.proposal: Knowledge addition in psychology-and-laws.md, alongside confirmation bias: an over-polished prototype reduces criticism; evaluate at an appropriate fidelity.
